cases.name: EF-REG-015 - Connected Finance "This month" total computes correctly for non-31-day months
cases.rationale: Regression for a confirmed fix: getFinanceSummary()'s month-bounded aggregate used a hardcoded '-31' upper bound, which Data Fabric 400'd on any month with fewer than 31 days.
cases.objective: Verify getFinanceSummary's month-bounded aggregate query succeeds and returns correct figures when the newest data month has 28, 29, or 30 days.
preconditions: Test Manager project and Change Regression set resolved
cases.syntheticData: Uniquely-tagged records in ExpenseFlow_Expense with ExpenseDate values spanning a 30-day month (e.g. September, matching current calendar month), including one dated on the month's actual last day (-30). One control record in a 31-day month for contrast.

steps.description: Seed the synthetic dataset; confirm retrievable via a fresh Data Fabric query.
steps.expectedResult: All seeded records, including the last-day-of-month record, are retrievable.

steps.description: Open Finance (connected) and let it load/refresh.
steps.expectedResult: No 400/error state on the summary call; page loads cleanly.

steps.description: Verify the "This month" count and total match the expected sum of seeded records for that month.
steps.expectedResult: Count and total are accurate for the 30-day month, including the last-day record.

negativeChecks: Confirm the 31-day-month control record is correctly excluded/included per its own date.
Confirm no prior '-31' upper-bound error resurfaces (check network/console for a 400 on the aggregate call).

cases.name: EF-REG-016 - Connected policy routing at the exact threshold boundary
cases.rationale: EF-REG-001 only tests below- and above-threshold amounts. policy.ts/NewExpenseForm.tsx route on strict '>', so an amount exactly equal to the threshold must stay auto-approved; an off-by-one regression here is untested.
cases.objective: Verify an expense amount exactly equal to the live policy threshold is auto-approved (not routed to manager approval).
preconditions: Known current policy threshold value read live before the test
cases.syntheticData: One synthetic expense with amount set to the exact current policy threshold value.

steps.description: Read the current policy threshold live (readPolicyThresholdNow equivalent) immediately before submission.
steps.expectedResult: Threshold value is recorded for the assertion.

steps.description: Submit the synthetic expense with amount == threshold in connected mode.
steps.expectedResult: Record is created with the below-threshold (auto-approved) outcome, not the approval-routing outcome.

steps.description: Read the created record through the app after refresh.
steps.expectedResult: Status and persisted policy note agree with the auto-approved path.

negativeChecks: Submit a second expense at threshold + smallest currency unit and confirm it DOES route to approval, confirming the boundary is exercised on both sides.

traceability.note: Coverage gap, not tied to a specific commit; extends EF-REG-001.

cases.name: EF-REG-017 - Policy threshold is read live at decision time, not from the display cache
cases.rationale: policy.ts documents a shipped bug (EXP-1014): the threshold Asset changed mid-session and a submission used the stale cached display value, writing a permanently wrong record. getPolicyThreshold() (cached, display-only) vs readPolicyThresholdNow() (live, decision-only) is the fix, but nothing regresses this by changing the Asset between page load and submit.
cases.objective: Verify that changing the policy threshold Asset after the New Expense form has loaded (and displayed the old threshold) still causes the submission decision to use the NEW value.
preconditions: Ability to change the ExpenseFlow_PolicyThreshold Orchestrator Asset for the test and restore it afterward
cases.syntheticData: One synthetic expense with an amount that is below the OLD threshold but above the NEW (lowered) threshold.

steps.description: Load New Expense with the current threshold; note the displayed threshold hint.
steps.expectedResult: Form shows the original threshold value.

steps.description: Without reloading the page, change the ExpenseFlow_PolicyThreshold Asset to a lower value.
steps.expectedResult: Displayed hint on the still-open form remains the old value (expected — it is cached for display).

steps.description: Submit the synthetic expense (amount between old and new threshold).
steps.expectedResult: The DECISION uses the new (live) threshold: the expense routes to approval, not auto-approved, even though the display still showed the old threshold.

steps.description: Restore the original Asset value.
steps.expectedResult: Threshold returns to baseline for subsequent tests.

negativeChecks: Confirm the persisted record's policy note reflects the threshold value actually used for the decision, not the one displayed at load.

traceability.note: Regression for historical bug EXP-1014, documented in policy.ts comments.

cases.name: EF-REG-018 - Sticky switches survive in-app navigation but not a hard reload
cases.rationale: StickySwitches.tsx exists because React Router's <Link> silently drops query params. No existing case exercises this component; EF-REG-012 only covers switches surviving OAuth-callback cleanup, a different code path.
cases.objective: Verify ?mock, ?demo, and ?simulateError persist across in-app (client-side) navigation via sidebar links, but do NOT survive a hard page reload.
preconditions: App reachable at verified local URL

steps.description: Load the app with a switch in the URL, e.g. ?demo=fail.
steps.expectedResult: Switch is active and present in the address bar.

steps.description: Click through several sidebar links (Dashboard -> My Expenses -> Approvals -> Finance) using in-app navigation only.
steps.expectedResult: The ?demo=fail param (or equivalent) reappears in the address bar after each navigation, and the switch remains behaviorally active.

steps.description: Use the browser Back button after several navigations.
steps.expectedResult: Back navigation works normally (no extra history entries were introduced by the switch being re-added).

steps.description: Manually remove the switch from the address bar and press Enter (hard load).
steps.expectedResult: The switch is now OFF — a hard reload does not resurrect a removed switch.

negativeChecks: Confirm a switch NOT present at initial load and never added does not spontaneously appear during navigation.

traceability.note: New coverage; component predates this scan but had no case.

cases.name: EF-REG-019 - Receipt upload sanitizes unsafe filenames
cases.rationale: receipts.ts's safeFileName() strips path separators and non-word characters (handles browser quirks like 'C:\fakepath\bill.pdf', spaces, '#'). EF-REG-004 uses a generic synthetic receipt filename and doesn't exercise this.
cases.objective: Verify a receipt uploaded with an awkward filename (spaces, '#', backslash-style segments, non-ASCII) is sanitized on upload and remains openable afterward.
preconditions: A synthetic receipt file with a deliberately awkward name, e.g. "Q3 Bill #4 (draft).pdf"
cases.syntheticData: One synthetic expense; receipt file named with spaces, a '#', and parentheses.

steps.description: Attach the awkwardly-named receipt to a valid connected expense and submit.
steps.expectedResult: Submission succeeds; the created record retains a receipt path that is a sanitized, bucket-safe name (no raw spaces/#/backslashes).

steps.description: Open the created expense detail and use its receipt link.
steps.expectedResult: Receipt opens correctly through authorized bucket access despite the original filename's unsafe characters.

negativeChecks: Confirm the stored path is still prefixed with the expense code (browsable in Orchestrator by code, per receipts.ts's documented intent).

traceability.note: Extends EF-REG-004 with an edge-case filename.

cases.name: EF-REG-020 - Error category maps to the correct recovery affordance
cases.rationale: errors.ts defines distinct UI affordances per error type (Authentication -> sign-in prompt, Authorization -> no action, Validation -> server-detail message, RateLimit/Server -> Retry button). EF-REG-009 only exercises one generic failure condition; a wrong-affordance regression (e.g. showing Retry for an expired session) is currently invisible.
cases.objective: Verify at least two distinct error categories each render their documented recovery affordance, not a generic error.
preconditions: Approved safe methods to trigger an authentication-expired condition and a validation-rejected condition without corrupting data
cases.syntheticData: One synthetic expense submission with a payload that trips server-side validation (e.g. a field Data Fabric rejects).

steps.description: Trigger an authentication-expired condition (session invalidated) and attempt an action.
steps.expectedResult: UI shows the 'session expired, sign in again' message with a Sign In affordance -- not a Retry button.

steps.description: Restore a valid session; trigger a validation-rejected submission.
steps.expectedResult: UI shows a message quoting the server's field-level detail, with no retry affordance offered (per errors.ts, Validation -> 'none').

steps.description: Restore normal conditions and confirm both flows recover cleanly.
steps.expectedResult: No raw provider exception is shown at any point in either flow.

negativeChecks: Confirm neither error path silently falls back to a generic 'something went wrong' message that loses the category-specific affordance.

traceability.note: Extends EF-REG-009 to assert on affordance correctness, not just presence of a friendly message.

cases.name: EF-REG-021 - Sign-out clears the session and returns to sign-in
cases.rationale: useAuth.tsx exposes logout() (calls sdk.logout()); no existing case touches sign-out -- every other case assumes an authenticated session throughout.
cases.objective: Verify using the sign-out affordance clears the authenticated session and returns the user to the sign-in/splash state, and that a protected route is no longer accessible without re-authenticating.
preconditions: Connected environment with an authenticated session established

steps.description: From an authenticated session, use the sign-out affordance.
steps.expectedResult: App returns to the sign-in/splash state; no application route renders.

steps.description: Attempt to navigate directly to a protected route (e.g. /finance) after sign-out.
steps.expectedResult: Route does not render authenticated content; user is prompted to sign in again.

steps.description: Sign in again.
steps.expectedResult: Session re-establishes and the app functions normally.

negativeChecks: Confirm no stale data from the prior session (e.g. cached Finance totals) is shown before the new session's data loads.

traceability.note: New coverage; no prior case touches sign-out.
